proof_attempt_summary: Discovery developed a count-selected, density-trimmed quadratic estimator with a stated uniform O(n^-1/2) MSE upper bound and transferred an n^-4/7 lower bound from an explicit positive-design subfamily. The independent D0.5 novelty review placed the result at subfield because the exact minimax exponent remains open and the lower construction does not isolate a density-zero obstruction. The two panel hygiene findings above remain unresolved; no Lean formalization was started.
tldr: The fully observable five-fold estimator has uniform mean-squared error \(O(n^{-1/2})\) for the eight-dimensional point-dose mean even when the marginal covariate density vanishes and only target-slice covariate regularity is available. Separately, when the fixed constants obey \(\overline P\ge1\) and \(0<c<1<C_{\pi}\), an explicit normalized fuzzy sign mixture inside the unchanged class proves the all-estimator lower bound \(c_0n^{-4/7}\), so \(1/2\le\gamma^\star\le4/7\) in that compatible strict-slack regime. The density-zero upper remains the field-novel headline; the exact minimax exponent remains open.
gap: The closest higher-order point-dose theorem reaches the desired numerical rate only with a positive localized design weight and an \(O(k)\) diagonal, while empirical-Gram higher-order theory also retains a positive design-density floor. Neither result covers a marginal density that can vanish under only target-slice covariate regularity.
fill: The estimator selects nuisance resolution by observed counts, learns normalizers on independent folds, deletes only the correction on cells with \(\widehat p<\tau\), and telescopes the dyadic kernel. The proposed lemmas reduce the proof to an exact four-term bias identity conditional on \(\mathcal T\), one explicit simultaneous good event with polynomial failure probability, \(L_q\) pilot moments for every \(q<11\), and an integrated cellwise second-moment bound. The uniform-design oracle reduction has bias exactly \(\theta_h-\theta\), so the projection contribution is correctly confined to variance in that special case.
